summary: The candidate correctly adds weighted non-blocking admission for tokenizer-owned multimodal preprocessing and passes its regression suite, but it acquires only after FastAPI/ASGI body buffering, request-model parsing, and base64 retention. Those explicitly reported pre-scheduler memory stages remain unbounded, so this is a partial fix rather than a complete resolution of the original CPU-OOM feature request.

tests.what_was_measured: With controller capacity 1 already occupied, 32 distinct parsed 4 MiB base64-like payloads remained allocated before 32/32 admission rejections; payload total 134217782 bytes and measured maximum-RSS growth 135076 KiB.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 was visible, but the changed code is CPU-side Python admission/accounting. No independent GPU numerical claim applies; Kimi-K2.6 weights and the reported 200-request/5600-image workload were unavailable.

native_rebuild_evidence: The candidate changes no C/C++/CUDA/HIP/FlyDSL/native or build-definition files. Source imports were verified from /job/repo/python. Existing cached AITER shared objects were observed but are not changed by this candidate.
remaining_counterexamples: Concurrent clients can each have their complete HTTP body buffered and parsed into request/base64 objects before TokenizerManager.generate_request attempts admission; memory in this stage is not bounded by --max-mm-preprocessing-inflight-items-per-worker.
The independent 32-request adversarial case retained approximately 128 MiB of payload data with a configured admission budget of one item, then rejected every request only after allocation.

The exact Kimi-K2.6, 200-concurrent-request, 28-images-per-request, 1.5 TiB host-memory failure was not reproducible because model weights and an equivalent host were unavailable, so end-to-end prevention of that OOM remains unverified.
The option is rejected for the Rust frontend and EPD language-only mode, leaving those architectures unsupported by this feature.
remaining_limitations: This review verifies tokenizer-side accounting and error propagation with unit tests, not semantic multimodal model accuracy.
No qualified multimodal model fixture or Kimi-K2.6 weights were available; the provided tiny Llama fixture is text-only and was intentionally not used as unrelated proof.
Two context-parallel server-argument tests are platform-inapplicable on HIP and fail independently of the candidate; both are retained in raw evidence and narrowly deselected in the applicable run.
No native rebuild was performed because no native source or build input changed.
